# Dockerfile for llm_studio on llama.cpp
# Environment: Python 3.10, with llama.cpp and llm_studio

FROM python:3.10-slim

# Set environment variables
ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    POETRY_NO_INTERACTION=1 \
    POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_IN_PROJECT=1

# Install system dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    curl \
    make \
    libomp-dev \
    libbz2-dev \
    liblzma-dev \
    libsqlite3-dev \
    python3-dev \
    python3-venv \
    && apt-get clean \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create project structure
WORKDIR /app

# Copy requirements first for better layer caching
COPY pyproject.toml poetry.lock* 2>/dev/null || true
COPY requirements.txt 2>/dev/null || true

# If requirements.txt exists, install dependencies
RUN if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then \
        pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt; \
    fi

# Install llm_studio
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir llm-studio

# Install llama.cpp dependencies
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir \
    torch \
    torchvision \
    torchaudio \
    --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu

# Install llama.cpp (C++ implementation)
RUN git clone https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp --depth 1 --recursive \
    && cd llama.cpp \
    && make -C build-python \
    && pip install --no-cache-dir build-python/install/

# Set up environment for llama.cpp
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/app/llama.cpp/build-python/install/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}
ENV PATH=/app/llama.cpp/build-python/install/bin:$PATH

# Create necessary directories
RUN mkdir -p \
    /app/llm_studio_config \
    /app/uploads \
    /app/models \
    /app/cache

# Copy application code
COPY . .

# Install additional utilities
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir \
    uvicorn \
    gunicorn \
    fastapi \
    gradio

# Create non-root user for security
RUN groupadd --gid 1000 appgroup \
    && useradd --uid 1000 --gid 1000 --shell /bin/bash --createhome appuser

# Change ownership
RUN chown -R appuser:appgroup /app

# Switch to non-root user
USER appuser

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Expose port for llm_studio web server
EXPOSE 8000

# Default command
CMD ["python", "-m", "llm_studio.train.cli", "--port", "8000", "--host", "0.0.0.0"]

# Dockerfile for llm_studio on llama.cpp

## Overview
This project provides a Docker setup for llm_studio, a web-based interface for training and inference on LLMs, running on top of llama.cpp.

## Quick Start

### Build the Docker Image
```bash
docker build -t llm_studio_llama .
```

### Run the Container
```bash
docker run -d \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -v ./models:/app/models \
    -v ./uploads:/app/uploads \
    -v ./cache:/app/cache \
    --name llm_studio \
    llm_studio_llama
```

### Access the Web Interface
Open http://localhost:8000 in your browser.

## Prerequisites for Building

### System Dependencies
Before building Docker image on Linux:
```bash
apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    libomp-dev \
    libbz2-dev \
    liblzma-dev \
    libsqlite3-dev \
    python3-dev \
    python3-venv
```

### Docker
Make sure Docker is running:
```bash
docker --version
docker run hello-world
```

## Directory Structure

- `Dockerfile` - Main build file
- `requirements.txt` - Python dependencies (optional, will be auto-generated)
- `pyproject.toml` - Poetry configuration (if used)
- `README_llm_studio.md` - This file

## Usage Examples

### Training a Model
```bash
# Prepare dataset in ./data
docker run -d \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -v ./data:/app/data \
    -v ./models:/app/models \
    llm_studio_llama \
    python -m llm_studio.train.cli \
    --port 8000 \
    --host 0.0.0.0
```

### Inference Only
```bash
docker run -d \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -v ./models:/app/models \
    llm_studio_llama \
    python -m llm_studio.inference.cli \
    --port 8000 \
    --checkpoint /app/models/model.gguf
```

## Configuration

### Environment Variables
| Variable | Description | Default |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| `PORT` | Web server port | 8000 |
| `HOST` | Host to bind | 0.0.0.0 |
| `NUM_GPU_LAYERS` | GPU layers for llama.cpp | -1 (all) |
| `NUM_THREADS` | CPU threads | -1 (all) |
| `MAIN_GPU` | Main GPU | -1 |

### Volume Mounts
| Mount | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `./models` | Store GGUF model files |
| `./uploads` | Training datasets |
| `./cache` | Intermediate files |
| `./logs` | Application logs |

## Security Notes

- Runs as non-root user (`appuser`)
- All dependencies installed with `--no-cache-dir`
- Read-only base image where possible

## Troubleshooting

### GPU Support
For CUDA support:
```bash
# Update base image
FROM python:3.10-cudatoolkit-12.1

# And rebuild with:
pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121
```

### Out of Memory
Reduce batch size or number of GPU layers:
```bash
export MAX_JOBS=4
export NUM_GPU_LAYERS=-1
```

### Build Cache Issues
Clean and rebuild:
```bash
docker builder prune
docker build --no-cache -t llm_studio_llama .
```

## Resources

- [llm-studio](https://llm-studio.ml)
- [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp)
- [ollama](https://github.com/ollama/ollama)

## License

CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

# Local AI Development Environment

## Overview

This is a comprehensive local AI development environment designed for data analytics, FEM/Blender integration, energy optimization engines, and computer vision/ML applications on embedded devices.

The project runs local LLMs via Ollama and provides MCP (Model Context Protocol) server support for various systems including:
- Blender for 3D modeling
- FEniCS/Dolphin for finite element calculations  
- Graph optimization engines
- Computer vision (pose estimation)
- Knowledge graphs

## System Specifications

### Operating System
- **Distro:** Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Noble Numbat)
- **Kernel:** 7.0.0-22-generic

### CPU
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Model** | AMD Ryzen 7 260 w/ Radeon 780M Graphics |
| **Cores** | 8 physical cores (16 threads with SMT) |
| **Architecture** | Zen 3 (Family 25, Model 117) |
| **Base Frequency** | Variable (417 - 5102 MHz boost) |
| **L1 Cache** | 256 KiB per core (8 instances) |
| **L2 Cache** | 8 MiB (8 instances) |
| **L3 Cache** | 16 MiB (shared) |
| **Virtualization** | AMD-V enabled |

### GPU / Display
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **GPU Model** | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 |
| **CUDA Version** | 13.2 |
| **Driver Version** | 595.71.05 |
| **VRAM** | 8 GiB (GDDR6) |
| **PCIe Device** | 00000000:01:00.0 |

### Memory
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Total RAM** | 30 GiB |
| **Available** | ~14 GiB |
| **Swap** | 11 GiB |

### Storage
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Total Size** | 761 GiB |
| **Used** | 610 GiB (85%) |
| **Available** | 113 GiB |
| **Filesystem** | overlay |

## Software Stack

### AI/ML Stack
- **Ollama:** ✓ Installed (local LLM serving)
- **CUDA:** ✓ Version 13.2
- **NVIDIA Drivers:** ✓ 595.71.05

### Development Tools
- **Python:** For AI/ML development (Python 3.10)
- **GCC/Clang:** For embedded development
- **Ansible:** For remote deployment (Jetson)
- **Docker:** For containerized services
- **FastAPI:** For web APIs
- **Gradio:** For web-based UI

## Project Components

### Main Development Areas

#### 1. FEM Analysis
- **Technology:** FEniCS, Dolphin
- **Use Case:** Heat transfer calculations
- **Directory:** `heat_fem/` (external project reference)

#### 2. Optimization Engine
- **Technology:** Graph-based optimization
- **Use Case:** Energy systems optimization
- **Directory:** `phys_opt/` (external project reference)

#### 3. Computer Vision
- **Technology:** Pose estimation, PyTorch vision models
- **Use Case:** ML models for embedded devices
- **Directory:** `pose_estimate_py/` (external project reference)

#### 4. Blender Integration
- **Technology:** MCP server for Blender
- **Use Case:** 3D modeling via LLM commands
- **Directory:** `blender_mcp/` (referenced in AGENTS.md)
- **Current:** `lav/src/blender_cv/` - Pose estimation for Blender

#### 5. Knowledge Graphs
- **Technology:** Local graph databases
- **Use Case:** Semantic reasoning and knowledge retrieval

#### 6. Web/ML Studio
- **Technology:** LLM Studio with llama.cpp
- **Use Case:** Web-based machine learning interface
- **Directory:** `home/sabeiro/`

### MCP (Model Context Protocol) Support

This environment provides MCP server capabilities for interacting with:

| System | Directory | Description |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| Blender | `blender_mcp/` | 3D modeling controls |
| FEM | `heat_fem/` | Finite element calculations |
| Optimization | `phys_opt/` | Energy optimization |
| CV | `pose_estimate_py/` | Computer vision models |
| KB | Knowledge graphs | Local knowledge base |

### Docker Support

Docker containerization for portable deployment:

**Dockerfile** (`home/sabeiro/Dockerfile`)
- Python 3.10 base image
- LLM Studio installation
- llama.cpp integration
- Non-root user for security
- Exposes port 8000 for web interface

**Build & Run Commands:**

```bash
# Build Docker image
docker build -t llm_studio_llama .

# Run container
docker run -d \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -v ./models:/app/models \
    -v ./uploads:/app/uploads \
    -v ./cache:/app/cache \
    --name llm_studio \
    llm_studio_llama

# Access web interface
# Open http://localhost:8000 in browser
```

### Ollama Setup

The environment includes:
- **Containerized Ollama** for local LLM serving
- **Model management** via `model_list.txt`
- **Direct HF URL downloads** (no token required for public models)
- **Compatible models:**
  - llama-3.1-8b-instruct
  - llama-3.2-3b-instruct
  - llama-3.3-70b-instruct
  - mistral-7b-v0.3
  - phi-3-mini-4k
  - qwen2.5-7b-instruct

### Emacs Integration

Emacs configuration for org-mode based development workflows:
- **Location:** `./emacs/`
- **Workflow:** Code execution via Python REPL and org-mode code blocks
- **Purpose:** Interactive data analytics without production code

## Deployment Options

### 1. Local Development
- Run directly on Ubuntu system
- Use docker-compose for service orchestration
- Accessible via localhost:8000

### 2. Remote Deployment (Jetson)
- **Tool:** Ansible playbooks in `ansible/`
- **Target:** NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Developer Kit
- **Capabilities:** 8GB RAM, ARM Cortex-A55 cores

### 3. Web Server
- **Location:** `nginx/` for web deployment
- **Purpose:** Deploy on Jetson or other servers

### 4. Monitoring
- **Tool:** MCP Hub in `mcphub/`
- **Purpose:** Monitor MCP applications

## Directory Structure

```
/home/sabeiro/
├── home/sabeiro/
│   ├── Dockerfile              # Main Docker build file
│   └── README_llm_studio.md   # LLM Studio specific docs
├── .pi/
│   ├── agent/                  # Pi coding agent configuration
│   │   ├── AGENTS.md          # Agent instructions
│   │   ├── config.json        # Agent configuration
│   │   ├── models.json        # Model list
│   │   └── settings.json      # Agent settings
│   ├── config.json            # Pi coding agent config
│   ├── llama-server.json      # Llama server config
│   ├── mcp_server.json        # MCP server config
│   ├── models.list            # Available models
│   ├── ollama.env             # Ollama environment
│   └── setup.txt              # Setup instructions
├── .ollama/                   # Ollama models and cache
├── .npm/                      # Node packages
├── Dockerfile                 # System container
├── docker-compose.yml         # Service orchestrator
└── pi-session-*.html          # Session logs
```

## Usage Examples

### Starting LLM Studio
```bash
docker run -d \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -v ./models:/app/models \
    -v ./uploads:/app/uploads \
    -v ./cache:/app/cache \
    --name llm_studio \
    llm_studio_llama
```

### Training a Model
```bash
docker run -d \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -v ./data:/app/data \
    -v ./models:/app/models \
    llm_studio_llama \
    python -m llm_studio.train.cli \
    --port 8000 \
    --host 0.0.0.0
```

### Running with Ollama
```bash
# Pull a model
ollama pull llama-3.2-3b-instruct

# Run inference
ollama run llama-3.2-3b-instruct "Hello, how are you?"
```

## Configuration

### Environment Variables
| Variable | Description | Default |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| `PORT` | Web server port | 8000 |
| `HOST` | Host to bind | 0.0.0.0 |
| `NUM_GPU_LAYERS` | GPU layers for llama.cpp | -1 (all) |
| `NUM_THREADS` | CPU threads | -1 (all) |
| `MAIN_GPU` | Main GPU | -1 |

### Volume Mounts
| Mount | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `./models` | Store GGUF model files |
| `./uploads` | Training datasets |
| `./cache` | Intermediate files |
| `./logs` | Application logs |

### Ollama Models
Available for download (without HF token):
- llamas, mistral, phi, qwen2.5
- Use `get_gguf_without_token.sh` scripts
- Or use direct HF URLs

## Security

- **Run as non-root user:** App user with restricted permissions
- **Read-only base image:** Where possible
- **Security context:** Docker labels with restricted:privileged=true:FALSE

## Troubleshooting

### Out of Memory
Reduce batch size or number of GPU layers:
```bash
export MAX_JOBS=4
export NUM_GPU_LAYERS=-1
```

### Build Cache Issues
```bash
docker builder prune
docker build --no-cache -t llm_studio_llama .
```

### GPU Support
For CUDA support in Docker:
```bash
FROM python:3.10-cudatoolkit-12.1
pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121
```

## Resources

- [LLM Studio Documentation](https://llm-studio.ml)
- [llama.cpp GitHub](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp)
- [Ollama GitHub](https://github.com/ollama/ollama)
- [FEniCS Documentation](https://fenicsproject.org/)

## License

## Owner

intertino

### Docker Support

Docker containerization for portable deployment:

- Exposes port 8000 for web interface

**Build & Run Commands:**

```bash
# Build Docker image
docker build -t llm_studio_llama .

# Run container
docker run -d \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -v ./models:/app/models \
    -v ./uploads:/app/uploads \
    -v ./cache:/app/cache \
    --name llm_studio \
    llm_studio_llama

# Access web interface
# Open http://localhost:8000 in browser
```

## Usage Examples

### Starting LLM Studio
```bash
docker run -d \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -v ./models:/app/models \
    -v ./uploads:/app/uploads \
    -v ./cache:/app/cache \
    --name llm_studio \
    llm_studio_llama
```

### Training a Model
```bash
docker run -d \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -v ./data:/app/data \
    -v ./models:/app/models \
    llm_studio_llama \
    python -m llm_studio.train.cli \
    --port 8000 \
    --host 0.0.0.0
```

### Running with Ollama
```bash
# Pull a model
ollama pull llama-3.2-3b-instruct

# Run inference
ollama run llama-3.2-3b-instruct "Hello, how are you?"
```

## Configuration

### Environment Variables
| Variable | Description | Default |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| `PORT` | Web server port | 8000 |
| `HOST` | Host to bind | 0.0.0.0 |
| `NUM_GPU_LAYERS` | GPU layers for llama.cpp | -1 (all) |
| `NUM_THREADS` | CPU threads | -1 (all) |
| `MAIN_GPU` | Main GPU | -1 |

### Volume Mounts
| Mount | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `./models` | Store GGUF model files |
| `./uploads` | Training datasets |
| `./cache` | Intermediate files |
| `./logs` | Application logs |

### Ollama Models
Available for download (without HF token):
- llamas, mistral, phi, qwen2.5
- Use `get_gguf_without_token.sh` scripts
- Or use direct HF URLs

## Security

- **Run as non-root user:** App user with restricted permissions
- **Read-only base image:** Where possible
- **Security context:** Docker labels with restricted:privileged=true:FALSE

## Troubleshooting

### Out of Memory
Reduce batch size or number of GPU layers:
```bash
export MAX_JOBS=4
export NUM_GPU_LAYERS=-1
```

### Build Cache Issues
```bash
docker builder prune
docker build --no-cache -t llm_studio_llama .
```

### GPU Support
For CUDA support in Docker:
```bash
FROM python:3.10-cudatoolkit-12.1
pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121
```
